title: Developer DX Quickstarts, Templates, and Canonical Fixes
author: Asha Iyer
body:
Overview

Purpose: This page is a single entry for Developer Experience (DX) owners and contributors that collects the canonical quickstarts, SDK usage patterns, docs-site operating procedures, and the most common support issues with canonical fixes. Use this as the working handbook for publishing and maintaining customer-facing quickstarts and API examples.

Audience: SDK engineers, technical writers, solutions engineers, and support engineers who maintain or use Redwood SDKs and quickstarts.

Maintainers and contact
- Primary owner: eng-dx (engineering)
- On-call DX rotation: see team wiki /confluence/eng-developer-experience/team-wiki/dx-oncall
- Doc reviewer cadence: quarterly or on SDK major/minor release

Quickstarts & templates (what to publish)
- Templates shipped from this directory:
  - quickstart-http-basic: Minimal HTTP curl + env-based API key example for first-time users.
  - quickstart-chat-react: React component pattern for streaming chat with optimistic UI.
  - quickstart-embeddings-pandas: Notebook template showing batch embeddings and vector index snapshot pipeline.
  - template-cli-tool: Pattern for wrapping Redwood API in a tiny CLI using click/argparse.

For each template include: one-sentence intent, supported SDKs, recommended audience, file list (README, example.env, snippets), and a smoke-test script. Example template README header: 

  # quickstart-chat-react
  Intent: show streaming chat + function-calling integration in a single-page app.
  Smoke test: npm start && curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/health"

SDK Guides (supported patterns and canonical snippets)
- Supported languages and versions:
  - Python (3.10+), official package: redwood-inference (pip install redwood-inference==<semver>)
  - TypeScript/Node (18+), official package: @redwood/inference
  - Go (1.20+), official module: github.com/redwood/inference-go
  - Curl/HTTP: canonical endpoints documented below for minimal integration.

- Canonical authentication pattern (env-first):
  1) Set REDWOOD_API_KEY in CI and local env.
  2) For private deployments, use REDWOOD_BASE_URL to point to private control plane.
  3) For sensitive customers, prefer token vault + short-lived tokens; include example for Okta/Azure token exchange.

Python example (canonical client usage):

  ```python
  from redwood_inference import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])
  resp = client.generate(model="redwood-alpha-1", prompt="Summarize the quarterly goals.")
  print(resp.text)
  ```

Node (streaming chat snippet):

  ```js
  import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
  const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', messages: [{role: 'user', content: 'Hello'}] })
  for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk.delta) }
  ```

API Examples (curl and error-tolerant patterns)
- Health check (curl):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health

- Minimal generation (curl):
  curl -X POST 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-small-1","prompt":"Translate to French: Hello"}' 
    https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate

- Best practices: use short timeouts, parse 429/503 to implement exponential backoff, stream where latency is important. Include request-id propagation (X-Request-ID header) for tracing.

Docs site operating procedures (publishing and lifecycle)
1) Drafting content
  - Create draft in the quickstarts directory with filename short-dashed and a one-paragraph description.
  - Add a reviewer from the reviewers list above.
  - Include smoke tests and CI job (see docs-ci/quickstart-smoke).

2) Review and verification
  - Technical review: SDK owner validates examples against latest package version.
  - Security review: Security team checks for credentials leakage and customer-specific endpoints.
  - Performance review (if template includes heavy calls): verify quota and rate-limit guidance.

3) Release checklist (before setting status -> published)
  - All code snippets run in isolated CI with environment variables pinned.
  - README contains purpose, expected outputs (sample), and lifetime support policy.
  - Labels: add at least [sdk, quickstart, language-<lang>].
  - Add related_pages links to product docs (model catalog, pricing).

4) Versioning and deprecation policy
  - Tag quickstarts with sdk-version and redwood-api-min-version metadata in header.
  - Deprecate templates after 12 months or after three major SDK releases without maintenance.
  - Announce deprecations on internal DX Slack channel and include migration guide.

5) Emergency hotfix process
  - If a published quickstart breaks critical onboarding (e.g., auth change), raise a docs-hotfix PR, run smoke-job with label "hotfix", and notify #dx-pager. Aim for 4-hour turnaround for critical fixes.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (operationally important)
- Issue: 401 / Invalid API key
  - Symptoms: 401 response, message: "Invalid API key" or "Unauthorized" in SDK.
  - Root cause: missing/expired API key, incorrect REDWOOD_BASE_URL (private customers).
  - Canonical fix: verify REDWOOD_API_KEY present and not prefixed with spaces; run `env | grep REDWOOD` and `curl -I -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" $REDWOOD_BASE_URL/v1/health`. For short-lived tokens, ensure token exchange succeeded.
  - Owner: support + sdk-team; runbook: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues/auth-runbook

- Issue: 429 or 503 during medium-volume batch embeddings
  - Symptoms: intermittent 429/503, partial batches returned.
  - Root cause: hitting per-account or per-deployment concurrency quota; burst without configured autoscaling.
  - Canonical fix: implement exponential backoff (base 250ms, multiplier 2, max 5s), batch size reduction, and enable job-level retry with idempotency tokens. Contact account SRE for quota increase for dedicated customers.
  - Owner: eng-sre + customer-success

- Issue: Streaming chunks appear truncated in browser UI
  - Symptoms: last chunk missing or decode errors in frontend; appears as incomplete UI reply.
  - Root cause: mixing newline boundaries and not handling chunked transfer encoding; dropped frames when using intermediate proxies.
  - Canonical fix: adopt the SDK streaming client (recommended) that reassembles deltas and verifies final token counts. For custom implementations: buffer until event terminator ("\n\n") and include request-id for logs.
  - Owner: eng-dx + frontend

- Issue: Model output quality regressions after model rollout
  - Symptoms: new model produces hallucinations or changes few-shot behavior in important prompts.
  - Root cause: model variant has different tokenizer or system prompt semantics; rollout missing canary tests.
  - Canonical fix: immediately rollback to previous pinned model, open a regression ticket linking prompt set and eval results, run quick local eval harness (see /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness) and escalate to model-onboarding.
  - Owner: applied-ml + eng-dx

- Issue: High tail latency for small, frequent requests
  - Symptoms: p95/p99 latency spikes, CPU/GPU context-switching observed.
  - Root cause: suboptimal batching policy; single-request throughput not tuned on dedicated fleets.
  - Canonical fix: enable continuous batching with max-latency 10ms and adjust small-request pool to prefer lower-latency nodes. Instrument token-level latency in Redwood Console and set alert at p95 > 250ms.
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime + eng-sre

Diagnostic checklist (quick triage)
1) Capture request-id and timestamps from the client.
2) Reproduce with curl using the same headers and body.
3) Check SDK version and compare semver against client compatibility table.
4) If streaming, confirm transfer-encoding headers and chunk boundaries.
5) If rate limit, add idempotency token and retry with exponential backoff.

Contributing guidelines for DX maintainers
- PR format: include smoke test results, annotated sample output in README, reviewer tag for each code-language.
- Labels: add language-, release-, and severity- labels.
- Documentation tests: add a small CI job that runs each quickstart smoke for at least Python and Node.
- Ownership handoff: update reviewers list when team members rotate.

Appendix: example smoke test (bash)
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -euo pipefail
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY="${REDWOOD_API_KEY:?set me}"
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \\  -d '{"model":"redwood-small-1","prompt":"Hello"}' \\  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate | jq -r '.text' | grep -i "hello"
